chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: The Opportunity Program and bringing parents into classrooms
summary: She explains how parent involvement became an Opportunity Program, with some teacher resistance.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Then of course with this Opportunity Program, they began to consider educational assistance. The educational assistance would have the opportunity to get involved in a Career Opportunity Program and pursue a course that would lead to an opportunity to teach actively. In the beginning the School Aids and the Family Workers were mostly elderly parents or maybe parents who were not considering getting involved in an educational career. But then we had a lot of young mothers who had probably stopped their education at some point to become parents and wanted to get back into it. So it was an opportunity for them to pursue a course and they could earn credits, and over a period they had different steps. They could become associates, etcetra, and work themselves right up the ladder. Where a young parent would have a lot of time in front of them to pursue a course like this. And as I said before there was a certain amount of resistance on the part of the teachers because the

teacher figured why should I have somebody in my classroom and I've gone through all these pains to get where I am and they're going to come in and take over my room. So you know how that would be. But anyway, now the Educational Assistant System Program is in full swing. We have alot of young parents who were started out as School Aids that are now full time teachers and some of the former School Aids are still School Aids, and some of them are still what they call Para-Professionals, Educational Assistants. Sometimes they work with a teacher under a specific program like remedial reading or remedial math, or work with the tudoring students that are a little behind in their grades. But I worked as an Educational Assistant and I - when I left the system I was operating as an Auxilary Trainer. That meant that I would be working with the potential teachers which was like early childhood education. But then I became a member of the Local School Board in District 12 here in the Bronx, and I served on a Local School Board for six years.
